theRuleAsImplemented.client: Each helper keeps its name and signature and gains an `*Answer` sibling returning RecordRailAnswer<T> = {form:"value", value} | {form:"absence", absenceVerdict:"absent-verified"|"not-applicable", reason} | {form:"refusal", code, reason} | {form:"current-path"}. `serve === "legacy-transitional"` is the ONLY producer of `current-path`, and `recordRailField(answer, substrate)` is the ONLY place a substrate value may be substituted.
theRuleAsImplemented.refusalCodes: The wire's four (`engine-refused`, `unaccounted`, `malformed-cell`, `no-such-parcel-or-rail`) are mirrored from the response's `refusal.code` when present. Two client-side codes exist because the client must not invent a finding the store did not make: `malformed-cell` for a `serve:record` cell whose kind this reader does not know, and `refusal-detail-missing` for `serve:refused` with no `refusal` object. Both are asserted, and the second is asserted NOT to be any of the wire's four.
theRuleAsImplemented.absenceIsAnAnswerNotASilence: On a slated rail a stated absence is the rail's answer: `absent-verified`/`not-applicable` carry the cell's own reason and the substrate is NOT substituted. This is the reading the fixture pins for those rows (form `absence`, with the verdict) and the one P-297's server implements.

designDecisions.fieldLevelVsSectionLevelRefusal: A refused rail suppresses its OWN field only. A section whose every rail is refused becomes `absent("refused")` — a stronger, different statement from `blocked-at-source`, because the ledger WAS asked and declined. `blocked-at-source` is now reachable only when no rail answered as a refusal.
designDecisions.sectionKindsPreservedForAbsence: Where a slated rail states an absence, the section keeps the kind the pre-cutover path used for a checked-empty answer (`clear` for specialDistricts, the existing absence kinds for utilities), because an unslated-equivalent absence is not a refusal and the two must not be reported identically.
designDecisions.cornerAxisCarveOut: An absence on the corner setback rail alone leaves cornerFt null and does NOT void the sheet; an absence on front/side/rear does. Reason: a district that publishes no corner standard is the ordinary case and the pre-existing export already treats a null corner as 'none published', whereas front/side/rear are required axes — substituting the corpus for them is exactly the retired behaviour. Asserted in both directions.
designDecisions.hifldNeverConsultedAfterARefusal: `utilities` has a second source (HIFLD) that the pre-cutover path used when the rail said nothing. After a slated refusal it is not consulted, and the test proves it by a resolver stub that would set a flag: it stays false and its holders never appear.
designDecisions.cityLimitsKeepsUnresolved: A refused cityLimits rail does not become `unincorporated` or `inside-city`: the honest status is `unresolved`, now carrying the ledger's code and reason on the new field rather than going silent.
designDecisions.whyKeepTheOldHelpers: Re-pointing all callers to the new unions in one commit would have forced edits to two pre-existing suites whose subject is not this defect. Keeping the wrappers (which return `value` or `undefined`) leaves them byte-identical in behaviour, and the ONLY production callers of the wrappers are now gone (verified: `rg` for non-Answer helper calls in production returns nothing).
